job.title: HSE contract opportunities | Accelerate your career I Enjoy flexibility
job.description:
Whether you are between permanent roles, looking for greater flexibility or intentionally building a diverse portfolio of experience, contracting can provide valuable career opportunities.

HSE Contract Opportunities | Join The Safe Step Contractor Network
With continued demand from our clients across Australia, The Safe Step is looking to connect with experienced Health, Safety and Environment professionals who are interested in current and future contract opportunities.

Whether you are between permanent roles, looking for greater flexibility or intentionally building a diverse portfolio of experience, contracting can provide valuable career opportunities.

Interested in discussing the contracting market or would like a confidential conversation about upcoming opportunities, reach out!

Why Contracting
Contracting is a great way to accelerate your career while enjoying variety and flexibility.

As a contractor, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Work across diverse industries, organisations and safety cultures
  • Build broad experience by contributing to major projects and business-critical initiatives
  • Make an immediate impact by applying your expertise where it's needed most
  • Develop your technical capability and leadership skills through varied assignments
  • Expand your professional network and strengthen your market profile
  • Choose opportunities that align with your career goals, lifestyle and preferred working arrangements
  • Access competitive remuneration while gaining exposure to some of Australia's leading organisations


Industry Exposure
Whether you're looking for a short-term assignment, project-based work or a longer-term contract, we partner with organisations that are committed to creating safer workplaces and value experienced HSE professionals who can make an immediate impact.
Our clients include leading organisations across:

  • Construction and Major Projects
  • Transport, Logistics and Supply Chain
  • Energy, Renewables and Utilities
  • Manufacturing and Industrial
  • Mining and Resources
  • Government and Public Sector
  • Healthcare and Community Services


Opportunities
We recruit and currently have a broad range of contract positions across Melbourne, with assignments varying from 6 weeks to 12 months across these levels:

  • HSE Coordinator
  • HSE Advisor
  • Senior HSE Advisor
  • Safety Business Partner
  • HSE Manager
  • Injury Management and Wellbeing professionals
  • Health and Safety Consultants
  • And Senior HSW Coaching opportunities


About You
We are keen to connect with professionals who:

  • Are immediately available or have a flexible notice period in your current role
  • Qualification in Work Health & Safety, Occupational Health, Environmental Management or a related discipline
  • Experience in a Health, Safety and/or Environment role
  • Strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation and contemporary risk management practices
  • The ability to build trusted relationships with operational and executive stakeholders
  • Excellent communication, coaching and influencing skills
  • Full Australian working rights

job.title: EGM Health, Safety, Security and Environment (HSSE)
Safety / HSEQ Administrator
job.description:
Join a business where compliance, safety and operational excellence matter
We are seeking a highly organised and detail focused HSEQ / Safety Administrator to support the ongoing management and continuous improvement of our Health, Safety, Environment and Quality (HSEQ) systems.

This is a pivotal role supporting the wider business through the administration of HSEQ systems, compliance processes, contractor onboarding, document control, reporting, training coordination, and regulatory compliance activities. You will work closely with operational teams, employees, contractors and external stakeholders to ensure our workforce remains compliant, competent and ready to deliver.

If you enjoy working with systems, managing critical documentation, analysing data and driving compliance outcomes, this is an excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation committed to continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain and continuously improve the Integrated Management System (IMS)
  • Administer the Lucidity HSEQ platform and other compliance systems.
  • Manage document control, registers, licences, certifications and training records.
  • Coordinate employee and contractor onboarding and inductions.
  • Monitor workforce competency requirements and track qualification renewals.
  • Manage client compliance portals and contractor compliance documentation.
  • Support audits, inspections, incident reporting and corrective action processes.
  • Produce HSEQ reports, dashboards, KPI reporting and trend analysis.
  • Support policy, procedure and SOP development and maintenance.
  • Coordinate HSEQ communications, awareness campaigns and monthly HSEQ initiatives.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • Previous experience in HSEQ administration, compliance coordination, document control or a similar support role.
  • Strong document management and records administration experience.
  • Experience using compliance management systems, digital platforms or HSEQ software.
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel and Word.
  • Experience using SharePoint or similar document management systems.
  • Strong analytical, reporting and data management capabilities.
  • Excellent organisational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
  • The ability to communicate effectively with stakeholders across all levels of the business.
  • A proactive approach and commitment to continuous improvement.

Why Apply?

  • Diverse and varied HSEQ role with broad business exposure.
  • Opportunity to work closely with senior leadership.
  • Play a key role in strengthening safety, compliance and operational performance.
  • Supportive team environment with opportunities to contribute to business improvement initiatives.
  • Stable and growing organisation with a strong commitment to safety and quality.

Apply Now
If you are a systems savvy administrator with a passion for compliance, organisation and continuous improvement, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today with your resume outlining your experience in HSEQ administration, compliance, document control or workforce and contractor compliance management.

job.title: WHS Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
The Safe Step is partnering with a large Canberra-based organisation to appoint an Interim WHS Manager. You’ll lead six direct reports within a nine-person team and partner closely with the head of WHS Operations as the organisation reviews how it delivers safety services.

The portfolio spans office-based and psychosocial risks through to specialist environments involving chemicals, hazardous materials, radiation and lasers. Your immediate priority is to give the team clear direction, work with stakeholders to understand what they need and make sure they receive consistent, practical WHS advice while the review is underway.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and develop the team. Set priorities, delegate effectively and coach WHS professionals with varying levels of experience. Build trust quickly and handle difficult conversations constructively.
  • Partner with operational leaders. Help them work through complex WHS issues, advise on risk controls and make sure the team follows through on agreed actions.
  • Support the service review. Bring forward stakeholder feedback, identify gaps in capability or service delivery and help the team adapt as changes are introduced.
  • Provide senior technical advice. Draw on your experience with WHS management systems, audits, assurance and complex incident investigations to support the team and advise senior leaders.

What you’ll bring
You’re an experienced WHS Manager or senior WHS leader with a track record of directly managing safety professionals in a complex organisation. You can show how you’ve coached a team, balanced competing demands and built credibility with leaders whose operations and risks differ considerably.
You’ll bring substantial WHS experience, including WHS management systems and complex investigations, backed by relevant qualifications or equivalent experience and training. Experience with chemicals, hazardous materials, radiation or other specialist high-risk environments is highly desirable. Tertiary or research-sector experience and ICAM accreditation would also be well regarded. Strong people leadership is the priority, and we welcome transferable experience from other complex sectors.

Apply now or reach out to Keilee Armstrong at The Safe Step karmstrong@thesafestep.com.au for a confidential conversation.

job.title: HSW Advisor
job.description:
About the Organisation
Our client is a well-established local government organisation based in Melbourne's South East, committed to delivering essential services to a diverse community. With a strong focus on employee wellbeing, operational excellence and continuous improvement, the organisation is looking to further strengthen its approach to workplace health and safety.

About the Role
Reporting to the Head of Health, Safety and Wellbeing, this is an excellent opportunity for an emerging HSE professional looking to further develop their experience in a diverse operational environment.

Working closely with leaders and employees across the organisation, you will play a key role in strengthening safety practices, building stakeholder capability and driving continuous improvement. This is a hands-on, people-focused role offering exposure to a diverse range of operational environments.
Key responsibilities include:

  • Provide practical HSE advice and guidance to leaders and employees.
  • Identify workplace hazards, conduct risk assessments and recommend appropriate controls.
  • Undertake workplace inspections, audits and safety assurance activities.
  • Support incident investigations, identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Coach and engage operational leaders to strengthen safety ownership and accountability.
  • Review and improve HSE policies, procedures and management systems.
  • Contribute to the delivery of safety initiatives, training and continuous improvement programs.

About You
We are looking for someone with a positive attitude, a genuine interest in health and safety and a willingness to learn. You don't need to have all the answers, but you will be someone who takes initiative, enjoys working with people and is motivated to develop their career.
To be successful, you will bring:

  • 1–3 years of experience in a health and safety role.
  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or other relevant qualifications.
  • A foundational understanding of WHS legislation and workplace risk management.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with people at all levels.
  • A proactive, practical and solutions-focused approach.
  • A willingness to learn, take on feedback and develop your technical knowledge.
  • A genuine passion for improving workplace safety and supporting others.

Experience within local government or a diverse operational environment would be advantageous, but is not essential.

What's on Offer
This is a fantastic opportunity for an early-career HSE professional to take the next step in their career. Offering hybrid working arrangements, exposure to a broad range of workplace environments and the opportunity to learn from experienced safety professionals, this role provides a great foundation for continued career development.

Apply Now

job.title: HSE Manager
job.description:
We are pleased to be partnering with Century Engineering to find an experienced and forward-thinking HSE Manager to join Century Engineering. With a proud 75 year history Century Engineering is one of South Australia's most established manufacturing and engineering businesses.

The organisation has built strong foundations in quality, safety and operational performance and is now focused on taking its safety, wellbeing and environmental outcomes to the next level. Reporting to the People & Culture Manager, you'll work closely with leaders and frontline teams to strengthen capability, embed continuous improvement and help shape the future of a high-performing and sustainable business.

The Opportunity
You will be instrumental in advancing the organisation's safety and environmental journey by:

  • Leading the ongoing development and enhancement of WHS and Environmental Management Systems aligned to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001.
  • Strengthening an already established safety culture through proactive risk management, wellbeing initiatives and continuous improvement programs.
  • Partnering with leaders and frontline teams to embed accountability, ownership and operational excellence across all levels of the business.
  • Driving continuous improvement through effective incident investigation, root cause analysis and corrective action management.
  • Championing environmental compliance, sustainability initiatives and responsible business practices that support long-term success.
  • Providing meaningful insights, metrics and reporting that inform decision-making and enhance organisational performance.

You'll Bring

  • Demonstrated success improving safety and environmental outcomes within manufacturing, industrial or other complex operational environments.
  • Experience developing, implementing and enhancing ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management systems.
  • A collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence, coach and positively challenge stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong expertise in risk management, incident investigation and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with a track record of building trust, credibility and buy-in across an organisation.
  • The ability to balance strategic thinking with a practical, hands-on approach to operational leadership.

Why This Role?

This is a unique opportunity to join a business with strong foundations and help shape its future direction. You'll have the autonomy and support to influence strategy, strengthen capability, advance culture and deliver measurable improvements for people, the environment and the business.

You'll be part of an organisation that values continuous improvement and recognises that sustainable success comes from empowering people, building capability and continually raising the bar.

If you're passionate about building on what's already working, while leading the transformation needed for tomorrow, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: HSEQ Project Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
An opportunity exists for an experienced HSEQ (Safety and Quality) Project Manager to lead safety, quality and environmental performance across a major greenfield commercial construction project in the Newcastle region.
This is a large, technically complex build with a substantial electrical construction and fit out component and a significant workforce expected on site through peak construction.
Sitting as part of the Project Senior Management Team, this is much more than a traditional site safety role. You will lead HSEQ across the project, providing direction across safety, quality, assurance, contractor management and operational risk from mobilisation through construction, fit out and commissioning.

The Role
Leading a dedicated project Safety and Quality team, your responsibilities will include:

  • Leading HSEQ performance across the project
  • Providing visible leadership across a large construction workforce
  • Leading and developing project safety and quality resources
  • Driving risk management, assurance and governance
  • Partnering with project leaders and contractors to improve WHSEQ performance
  • Providing oversight of quality processes across complex electrical construction and fit out
  • Supporting HSEQ systems, processes and continuous improvement
  • Contributing as a key member of the senior project leadership team

About You
We are looking for an established HSEQ professional with experience across major construction, electrical, engineering or infrastructure projects.
You will ideally bring:

  • Strong project based safety leadership experience
  • Exposure to electrical construction, fit out or complex building services
  • Experience within large greenfield construction environments
  • Genuine Quality and assurance capability
  • Experience leading HSEQ or project safety teams
  • Strong contractor and stakeholder management capability
  • The credibility to influence senior project and operational leaders

Electrical construction experience would be highly regarded, particularly across large commercial builds, complex electrical installations or highly serviced facilities.

job.title: Work Health and Safety Coordinator I AHCSA
job.description:
About the organisation
As the health voice for Aboriginal people in South Australia, AHCSA advocates for communities and our Member Services, supporting the delivery of culturally appropriate health programs grounded in a holistic understanding of health and wellbeing.

“Our Health, Our Choice, Our Way” is at the heart of AHCSA's identity, reflecting its commitment to Aboriginal self-determination, cultural safety and strengthening the Aboriginal community-controlled health sector. Guided by the principle of Aboriginal health in Aboriginal hands, AHCSA is committed to supporting Aboriginal people and communities to have a voice in decisions affecting their health and wellbeing.

About the opportunity
AHCSA is seeking an experienced Work Health and Safety professional to lead and strengthen its approach to workplace health, safety and wellbeing.

This is an opportunity to make a genuine difference in an organisation where psychological safety, cultural respect and employee wellbeing are just as important as legislative compliance.

Working across the organisation and with Member Services, you will build relationships, develop capability and ensure WHS practices are practical, accessible and responsive to the needs of AHCSA's people.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead the development, implementation and continuous improvement of AHCSA's WHS Management System, policies and procedures.
  • Manage WHS governance, risk assessments, audits, incident investigations and regulatory compliance.
  • Identify and manage psychosocial hazards, strengthening psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • Embed cultural safety principles into WHS practices, recognising the importance of cultural identity, lived experience and community.
  • Chair the WHS Committee and provide advice and guidance to senior leaders and employees.
  • Coordinate WHS training, inductions, reporting and Return to Work activities.
  • Build capability and encourage employee engagement in workplace health and safety.

About you
You will bring sound technical WHS knowledge and experience, together with the interpersonal skills, cultural awareness and judgement to work effectively within AHCSA.

You are approachable, a good listener and someone who takes the time to build genuine relationships and understand different perspectives. You recognise that creating a safe workplace goes beyond policies and procedures, and that trust, respect and open communication are fundamental to achieving positive outcomes.

You will bring:

  • Experience or demonstrated capability in psychosocial risk management, psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • The ability to engage respectfully with Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal employees, leaders and stakeholders.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to provide advice and constructively challenge when required.
  • A practical, collaborative approach to problem-solving, continuous improvement and building WHS capability.


A Diploma of Work Health and Safety, or Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety with substantial demonstrated experience at coordinator level, is essential.

Experience within community cantered environment will be highly regarded.

Why join AHCSA?
AHCSA offers the opportunity to contribute to an organisation making a meaningful difference to Aboriginal health and wellbeing across South Australia.

Along with a supportive, culturally respectful and purpose-driven workplace, benefits include:

  • Generous not-for-profit salary packaging.
  • Two additional weeks of paid leave over the Christmas period.
  • Four weeks of annual leave with 17.5% leave loading.
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Flexible working arrangements and professional development support.


How to apply
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

Cultural knowledge, lived experience and community connections are recognised and valued.

Applications are also welcomed from people of all backgrounds who demonstrate the experience, cultural awareness and commitment to AHCSA's values required for this position.

To apply, please submit your resume and a covering letter outlining your interest and relevant experience.

job.title: Health and Safety Business Partner
job.description:

job.title: HSEQ Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity

Our client is an established and growing essential services business operating across multiple sites, providing critical services to customers across a diverse operational environment.

With a busy workforce, multiple operational locations and a combination of transport, plant and site based activities, health and safety is an important part of how the business operates. The organisation is continuing to strengthen its approach to HSEQ, creating an opportunity for a Coordinator or developing Advisor to join the team and play a key role in that journey.

This is a broad, hands on position with exposure across operational health and safety, risk, incidents, compliance, audits, systems and improvement projects. There is plenty to do and plenty to learn, making it well suited to someone who wants more responsibility and broader experience.

Importantly, you will work closely with an exceptional leader who is approachable, supportive and genuinely invested in developing people. You will have someone to learn from and bounce ideas off, while being given the autonomy to build confidence and take greater ownership over time.

What You'll Do

  • Support day to day health, safety, environment and compliance activities across operational sites
  • Work with operational teams on risk assessments, controls and safety improvements
  • Support incident investigations and ensure actions are followed through
  • Coordinate workplace inspections, audits and compliance activities
  • Support the continued development and implementation of HSEQ systems and processes
  • Work closely with leaders, supervisors and frontline teams to strengthen safety engagement
  • Assist with training, injury management and broader HSEQ initiatives
  • Maintain safety documentation, records and compliance requirements
  • Help work through existing compliance priorities and keep actions moving
  • Contribute to projects and improvement initiatives as the safety function continues to develop

What You Bring

  • Experience in a health and safety role, ideally within an operational environment
  • A relevant health and safety qualification
  • An approachable, practical style and the confidence to build relationships across the business
  • Strong organisation skills with the ability to work through competing priorities
  • Curiosity and a genuine willingness to learn and develop
  • Initiative and the confidence to take ownership while remaining open to guidance
  • Good judgement and the ability to understand what needs attention first
  • Comfort balancing time in the operation with compliance and administration
  • A genuine interest in people and improving safety outcomes
  • The ability to work through ambiguity without needing every process or answer already mapped out

Experience across waste, transport, logistics, manufacturing, chemicals or another operational environment would be beneficial, but is not essential.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

There are two real drawcards to this opportunity: the leader and the breadth of the role.

You will work with a highly regarded health and safety leader who genuinely enjoys developing people and will give you the support, guidance and exposure to keep building your career.

You will also join a health and safety function that is continuing to evolve. Not everything is finished or perfectly established, and that is part of the opportunity. You will be able to get involved in a wide range of work, contribute ideas and build experience across areas you may not currently have exposure to.

About applying

For a confidential discussion, please contact Jai Catrios at jcatrios@thesafestep.com.au

job.title: HSE Advisor
job.description:
The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to join a growing renewable energy business with an expanding portfolio of projects and operational assets across Australia.

Working across development, construction and operations, the HSE Advisor will provide practical support and guidance to project teams, operational leaders and contractors across the business.

The role has a strong focus on contractor management, risk and assurance, while also supporting incident management, reporting, HSE systems and broader improvement initiatives. Rather than building from scratch, you will be joining a business with established frameworks and standards that now need to be consistently applied as the organisation and its portfolio continue to grow.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner with project, development and operational teams to provide practical HSE advice and support
  • Strengthen contractor management, oversight and assurance across projects and operational assets
  • Support risk management activities and ensure key HSE risks are understood and effectively managed
  • Participate in incident investigations, reviews and corrective actions, ensuring learnings are carried through the business
  • Coordinate audit and assurance activities and support the close out of identified actions
  • Contribute to HSE performance reporting, including monthly and board reporting
  • Support the consistent application of existing HSE policies, standards and management systems
  • Build the confidence and capability of leaders and teams to take greater ownership of safety
  • Identify practical opportunities to simplify and improve HSE processes as the organisation continues to evolve

What You Bring

  • Strong HSE experience gained within renewable energy, infrastructure, construction, utilities or another project and asset focused environment
  • Experience working across construction projects, operational assets and contractor environments
  • Sound technical capability across HSE management systems, risk, incidents, audits and assurance
  • A practical approach with the ability to balance HSE requirements with commercial and operational priorities
  • Strong relationship building skills and the credibility to work effectively with contractors, project teams, operational leaders and senior stakeholders
  • The ability to influence outcomes and build safety ownership through engagement
  • Confidence working autonomously across multiple priorities and geographically dispersed stakeholders
  • A continuous improvement mindset and the ability to operate comfortably within a growing and evolving organisation
  • Relevant qualifications in Work Health and Safety, Environmental Management or a related discipline

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a broad HSE role offering exposure well beyond a single construction project or operational site.

You will work across the lifecycle of renewable energy assets, partnering with teams across development, construction, operations and asset management while gaining visibility across a growing national portfolio.

The business already has solid HSE foundations in place. The opportunity is to strengthen how these are applied in practice, improve contractor assurance and help leaders take greater ownership of safety as the organisation grows.

For someone looking to broaden their renewable energy experience, work with a diverse group of stakeholders and contribute to a business going through continued growth, this offers plenty of variety and scope.

About Applying For further information or a confidential discussion, please contact Jai Catrios at The Safe Step.

Alternatively, click Apply for this job to submit your application.

 If you are an experienced HSE professional looking for an opportunity to take ownership of safety across a technical, operational environment and make a tangible impact, we would welcome your application.
